learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparing numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected one token and locked the prediction for unhappiness with available un, happi and ness pieces plus single letters.
observations.exploration: Initial segmentation was un, happi, ness: three tokens. Removed happi: seven tokens. Removed un: eight. Removed ness: eleven single-letter tokens. Selected zyxxy: five letters and five tokens. The history retained the original three and no-piece eleven cases.
observations.reveal: The reveal reset the stage to the original vocabulary and explicitly said so. It accurately quoted all-pieces three, no-pieces eleven and zyxxy five, explained model input as piece numbers, and connected vocabulary availability to frequent chunks in real tokenizer training.
observations.visual: Inspected the inline dark 1257 by 936 screenshot with all pieces enabled. Three large purple boxes showed un, happi and ness, each with a clearly invented numeric identifier. The toy label, vocabulary toggles, three-token count and history were legible.
observations.isolation: No-history evaluation preview banner present. Visible trust count ignored.
observations.reference: Own CUA tab 543884163 snapshots and inspected inline screenshot; no screenshot file saved.

prediction.reason: The question distinguishes written words from model input units under an explicit rule.
prediction.evidence: Selected one token despite the available three-piece vocabulary.

interaction.reason: Vocabulary toggles isolate why segmentation changes while spelling stays fixed.
interaction.evidence: The same word changed from three to seven, eight and eleven tokens.

payoff.reason: The reveal accurately uses the explored contrasts and explicitly discloses its reset.
payoff.evidence: It compares eleven letters in three tokens with five letters in five tokens.

clarity.reason: Chunk boxes, counts and history make segmentation visible.
clarity.evidence: Each piece has a separate box and made-up identifier.

transfer.reason: The ending applies the toy mechanism to interpreting real model input with a vocabulary condition.
transfer.evidence: Real tokenizers learn frequent chunks; what the model receives depends on that piece list.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard, focus, contrast audit, phone, zoom/reflow and motion unknown.

surprise.reason: A longer word can use fewer tokens than a shorter unfamiliar string.
surprise.evidence: Eleven letters used three tokens while zyxxy used five.

visualExplanation.reason: The boxes expose token boundaries and their change under vocabulary removal.
visualExplanation.evidence: One middle chunk becomes five letter units when disabled.

playfulness.reason: Switching vocabulary pieces on and off creates a direct segmentation toy.
playfulness.evidence: Three toggles alter the same word without editing it.

practicalValue.reason: It clarifies why word and character counts do not determine token count.
practicalValue.evidence: The reveal connects segmentation to a model's piece vocabulary.

depth.reason: The lesson separates spelling, segmentation, token IDs and vocabulary source.
depth.evidence: The reveal explains frequent chunks and model input numbers.

complexity.reason: The word pieces are familiar, but vocabulary-based encoding and token identifiers are new.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Moderate: distinguish a word from a sequence of vocabulary-dependent units.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Low: three toggles and two word choices.
complexity.conceptualChallenge: Input length in tokens depends on reusable chunks rather than visible word length.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Tokenizers, vocabularies and piece IDs are introduced.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Low to moderate: segmented text and invented numeric identifiers.

whyCool: The exact same spelling can become a different number of model-readable units when its piece list changes.
caveat: This is an explicit longest-piece toy with made-up IDs, not an audit of any actual production tokenizer.
missingEvidence: No user-entered fresh text or real tokenizer was tested.
